Subject: 1M-token target & latency-tier options — next steps

Hi Samir / procurement team — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick written recap and a couple of asks so we can get a pilot scoped out.

Summary from call:
- Target monthly volume for pilot: ~1,000,000 tokens (inbound + generated).
- Two distinct UX flows: critical real-time lookups (~20% of traffic) and async batch enrichment (~80%).
- Critical flow: desire p95 latency <= 300ms; batch flow can tolerate up to ~600ms.
- Security: SOC 2 and data isolation are must-haves for procurement.

What we need from you to finalize a scoped pilot:
1) Confirm the 1M/month target and expected growth cadence (months 1–6).
2) Confirm whether the critical flow must be strictly <=300ms p95 or if 350ms is acceptable near term.
3) Procurement contact for PO/SOW (name + email).

Attached is a first-pass pricing spreadsheet with three pricing bands and a hybrid routing suggestion. High-level unit economics we discussed on-call: target ~ $50–$80 per 1M tokens blended for pilot (depends on reserved capacity and streaming ratio).

Next steps proposed:
- You confirm the items above by EOD Thursday.
- We prepare a 2-week pilot proposal (technical runbook + pricing sheet + SOC2 artifacts).
- Procurement/Legal review SOW and sign PO to kick off.

Attachments: redwood-pricing-1M-token-proposal.xlsx (pricing bands), latency-slo-comparison.png (p95 examples)

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if that’s easier.

Best,

Subject: Re: 1M-token target & latency-tier options — next steps

Ben — thanks for the recap and the call. Confirming a few items from our side: we’re comfortable starting the pilot at 1M tokens/month. We expect headroom to double by month 3 if the pilot is successful.

Budget: our procurement lead gave a ballpark range for the pilot of $4k–$10k/month. That said, the product team is clear that for the critical flow we need p95 under ~300ms. If hitting that requires a premium, we need a clear breakdown of incremental $/1M tokens for the low-latency path vs standard batch.

Operational constraints:
- We will need SOC 2 Type II evidence and IP/credential handling specifics for the private VPC option.
- Procurement contact: Priya Menon (priya.menon@lumenworks.ai). She’ll own PO and SOW details.

If you can provide a couple of concrete pricing options (streaming/low-latency tier, batch/standard tier) and an estimate for a hybrid split (e.g., 20% streaming / 80% batch) that would help unblock our internal approval. Also include any recommended optimizations to lower unit cost (quantization, prefix caching, rate-limited batching).

—Samir
Samir Rao

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: RE: 1M-token target & latency-tier options — next steps

Samir — thanks, and great to have Priya as procurement contact. Below are two concrete pricing paths and our recommended hybrid approach. I’m keeping this high-level; full line-item numbers are in the attached spreadsheet.

Option A — Low-latency (streaming) tier — target p95 <= 250–300ms:
- Best for interactive flows (20% of traffic).
- Infrastructure: small dedicated reserved pool (streaming-optimized kernels, higher GPU utilization).
- Price: $180 per 1M tokens (includes reserved capacity amortization + priority routing).
- Pros: consistent p95, lower tail variability.
- Cons: higher $/token.

Option B — Standard (batch) tier — target p95 <= 600ms:
- Best for enrichment/async workloads (80% of traffic).
- Infrastructure: autoscaled batch workers with aggressive batching / prefix caching.
- Price: $40 per 1M tokens (on-demand, quantization friendly).
- Pros: low unit cost.
- Cons: higher latency, less consistent tail.

Recommended hybrid routing (pilot):
- 20% traffic -> Option A (streaming)
- 80% traffic -> Option B (batch)
- Blended estimated unit cost: (0.2 * $180) + (0.8 * $40) = $68 per 1M tokens.

Optimizations to reduce effective unit cost:
- Prefix/KV cache for repeated prompts (~15–30% token reduction on many flows).
- Model quantization suggestion for batch tier (int8) with negligible quality loss for enrichment tasks.
- Short KV caches for streaming to reduce autoregressive tokens where applicable.

Pilot commercial ask:
1) Pilot term: 2 weeks technical + 4 weeks run at target volumes (we can scale down if you prefer).
2) Pilot discount: we can offer a 10% pilot discount on the blended rate for the initial month, then revert to standard.
3) Deliverables: SOW, SOC2 artifact packet, pilot runbook + monitoring dashboard access.

If that looks reasonable I’ll send a formal pilot SOW and updated spreadsheet with monthly line items and expected invoices (attached: redwood-pricing-1M-token-proposal.xlsx).

Best,
Ben Carter
